summary: **Parties Present:** Shri Venkatesh, Advocate, ACME Shri Shryeshth Sharma, Advocate, ACME Shri Suhael Bhuttan, Advocate, ACME Shri Vedant Choudhary, Advocate, ACME Shri Shubham Arya, Advocate, CTUIL Ms. Reeha Singh, Advocate, CTUIL Shri Harshvardhan, Advocate, CTUIL Shri Rishabh Saxena, Advocate, CTUIL Ms. Priyansi Jadiya, CTUIL Ms. Kavya Bhardwaj, CTUIL Shri Lashit Sharma, CTUIL Ms. Muskan Agarwal, CTUIL - _b) Set aside the Impugned Letter dated 10.07.2024 issued by Respondent No. 1 to Petitioner wherein the Respondent No. 1 has rejected the application for Petitioner’s Solar Plant connectivity to ISTS, and_ - _c) Hold that the LoA submitted by the Petitioner to the Respondent No. 1 is within the meaning and ambit of LoA as required under Regulation 5.8 (xi) (a) of the GNA Regulations, and_ - _f) pass such further Order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit in the facts and circumstances of the present case._ - _a) Petitioner is seeking interim relief from this Hon’ble Commission to direct Respondent No. 1 to reserve the capacity of 2182 MW at Sanchore S/s being subject to the outcome of the present Petition._ - _d) Pass any other order or direction as it may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case._ - h. On 05.06.2024, CTUIL raised certain queries pertaining to the Petitioner’s application as under: - i. On 06.06.2024, the Petitioner, _vide_ its letter, made a detailed response to the queries raised by the CTUIL as under: - l. In view of the above stated facts and circumstances, the Petitioner has been constrained to approach this Commission, seeking the indulgence of this Commission, to exercise its power to regulate under Section 79 (1)(c) of the Electricity Act, 2003 and issue appropriate direction(s)-cum-clarification under Section 79(1)(c) of the Electricity Act, 2003 among other applicable law(s) _inter alia_ to the effect that the LoA dated 02.02.2024 and addendums to the LoA issued by SECI to Petitioner as the successful bidder has been issued pursuant to the Competitive Bidding process undertaken by SECI and the LoA submitted by the Petitioner to CTUIL for grant of connectivity is for the purposes of supply of power from its Solar Plant to its Green Hydrogen Plant and qualifies as an LoA within the scope of LoA as provisioned under Regulation 5.8 (xi) (a) of the GNA Regulations. _“(c) The Petitioner to furnish the following information details/ clarification, on affidavit, within two weeks:_ _4. Insofar as the Petitioner’s prayer for grant of interim relief(s) is concerned, the Commission declined to issue any direction at this stage prior to considering the views of the Respondents on the above-noted aspects.”_ _5. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties, the Commission directed as under:_ _(a) The Petitioner to furnish the following details/clarification, on an affidavit within two weeks:_ - _(iii)The Petitioner to submit the quantum of the GNA that it has applied or would be applying for drawl of power for its Green Hydrogen plant in Orissa. The Petitioner to clarify the reasons for the non-application of the GNA for drawl, whereas it had made an application for the connectivity for the renewable project planned to supply power to such drawal._ _“Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner, ACME, has filed its compliance affidavit dated 21.9.2024 furnishing the additional information/clarification as sought by the Commission vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 22.8.2024. Learned counsel referred to the said affidavit and mainly submitted as follows:_ _(a) The Petitioner has already carried out various activities in relation to the setting up of its Green Hydrogen Plant (GHP) and solar project and has spent over approximately 150 crores towards such activities._ _3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner pointed out that in terms of the bid document, the Petitioner had a right to choose the location(s) of its RE Projects, and the location of Sanchore, Rajasthan, has been selected in order to ensure that its GHP is globally price competitive. He also added that even under the Mode-I of implementation modes, the selection of the developer is on the basis of the competitive bidding process. He again urged to pass an interim direction against any further allocation of capacity at Sanchore S/s._ _5. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission directed the Petitioner to furnish the following information/clarification, on affidavit, within three weeks:_ _“At the outset, the counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner has already applied for the connectivity for its 2182 MW of Solar Plant on Land + Bank Guarantee route [i.e., Regulation 5.8(xi)(c)] and is now only urging the Commission to relax (i) the_ _timeline for the submission of 50% land documents under Regulation 5.8(xi)(c) read with Regulation 11A of the GNA Regulations to 30 months from the date of in-principle grant of connectivity by CTUIL, and (ii) the requirement of submission of Bank Guarantee under Regulation 5.8(xi)(c) of the GNA Regulations to 2 lakhs/MW. The counsel submitted that the Petitioner has already filed its affidavit to the above effect, which may be considered by the Commission, and the matter may, accordingly, be reserved for the order._ 14. The Petitioner vide affidavit dated 22.05.2025 has mainly submitted as under: 19. We have considered the submission of Petitioners, Respondent and facts on record. The following issues arise for our consideration: 39. Considering the above, we are not inclined to consider the request for reducing the quantum of BG for the Petitioner. We note that the arrangement of land is the first and prime requirement for the implementation of the generating station, and accordingly, Regulation 11A(1) requires the submission of the land documents. 42. Issue No. 2 is answered accordingly. All the Prayers of the Petitioner are rejected accordingly.
